title: Evolving Together, Failing Apart: The Skill-Policy Co-evolution Trap in Self-Improving Agents

object.carrier: delivered pair: a co-evolved policy checkpoint plus its final skill bank (the delivered bank) — textual skill records injected into the policy context; after deployment the bank keeps drifting (rewrites, additions, removals) while the policy stays fixed

safety_property.statement: The paper studies reliability degradation of self-improving agents under post-deployment skill drift (success rate, consistency under meaning-preserving rewrites, resistance to corrupted skills), not a security property. No adversary exists: drift is benign or accidental, and the corrupted-skill axes (T2/T3) are audit stimuli generated by the released suite inside the harness, not attacks. Per the SCOPE rule, pure reliability degradation under benign drift is not treated as a safety endpoint here; the value to this survey is as necessary background on how self-improving agent state (skill bank) and policy co-specialize and then fail apart.
safety_property.operationalized_as: CODA metrics: net-benefit gate Δnet = SR(S*) − SR(∅); consistency rate CR vs two-run noise floor CR0; resistance rate RR_T2/RR_T3; worst-case success SR_min over T1-T3; verdict = absolute within-method pass/fail

assumptions: skill banks are non-stationary after deployment: skills are rewritten, entries added or removed, versions coexist, often faster than the policy is retrained

theory (Proposition 1) assumes idealized cooperative acceptance (Assumption 1) and candidate coverage of the content-level neighborhood (Assumption 2); predictions are tested only for the covered rewrite family T1-T3 with retrieval/selection masked
one co-evolution run per setting; each method is audited on the bank it delivered, with the rewriting model, version and sampling pinned and perturbed banks released
not_covered: no adversary: no attacker optimizes the drift; corrupted skills are produced by the audit suite, not a malicious party
arbitrary post-deployment edits outside the covered content-level family — structural axes T4 (ecosystem) and T5 (autonomy) are reported but not scored
mitigation: the paper diagnoses but does not fix (Limitation L2)
variability across training seeds (single run per setting) and exact Mind2Web/AMC23 task counts (left to released configuration)

intervention.name: CODA (CO-evolution Drift Audit)
intervention.description: A deployment-oriented audit protocol, not a mitigation: it audits the delivered policy-bank pair with a shared external rewriting suite (gpt-4o-2024-08-06, temperature 0.7, pinned; released perturbed banks, selection masking R1-R5), scores worst-case success (SR_min), consistency (CR vs CR0) and resistance (RR_T2/RR_T3) behind a net-benefit gate, and returns an absolute within-method pass/fail verdict. Limitation L2 states the paper proposes no mitigation for the trap it measures.

controls.name: CR0 consistency between two unperturbed runs (decoding-noise floor)
20 identity pairs (skill vs itself) in T1 meaning-preservation audit
40 negative controls (skill vs its T2/T3 rewrite) in T1 meaning-preservation audit
pure-RL arm A on SkillRL-ALFWorld with the skill mechanism disabled throughout

results.claim: Across four co-evolution methods and five benchmarks (six settings), worst-case success under tested content-level skill drift (lowest of T1-T3) is 5-13 points below the peak measured for each delivered pair, erasing 52-93% of the delivered bank's gain over the no-skill baseline; the reported peak overstates deployable competence.

results.setting: final delivered pairs of SkillRL, ReSkill, Evolving-RL, ARISE on ALFWorld, WebShop, ScienceWorld, Mind2Web, DeepScaleR-AMC23 (six method-environment settings), re-evaluated under one fixed CODA protocol
results.quote: Across four co-evolution methods and five benchmarks (six settings), worst-case success is 5–13 points below the peak measured for each delivered pair, erasing 52–93% of the delivered bank’s gain over the no-skill baseline.

results.claim: Sensitivity to skill drift grows as co-evolution training proceeds: at least one content-level axis has a significantly positive absolute-Drop slope in five of six settings (SkillRL-WebShop is the sole exception), and twelve of the eighteen axis-setting pairs are significant, four on each of T1, T2 and T3.

results.comparison: twelve of eighteen axis-setting pairs significant

limitations.statement: L1: rewriting is not bit-reproducible, and if the bank was written by the same model family that later rewrites it, measured fragility may be optimistically low.
limitations.quote:
If the bank was
written by the same model family that later rewrites it, the measured fragility may be
optimistically low.

limitations.statement: L2: the work diagnoses but does not fix — it exposes fragility and provides a measurement tool but proposes no mitigation.
limitations.quote:
We diagnose but do not fix. We expose the fragility and provide a
measurement tool, but propose no mitigation.

limitations.statement: L3: scale is unstudied — whether broader exposure (more benchmarks, larger banks, more data) reduces wording sensitivity or merely raises the peak is beyond the paper's design.
limitations.quote:
Scale is unstudied. Whether broader exposure—more benchmarks,
larger banks, more data—reduces sensitivity to wording or merely raises the peak from
which the worst case falls away is beyond our design, and is the most interesting open
question beyond the fix itself.

limitations.statement: Each setting comes from a single co-evolution run, so reported bands quantify evaluation noise only, not variability across training seeds.
limitations.quote:
Each setting comes from a single co-evolution run, so the bands quantify
evaluation noise, not variability across training seeds.
limitations.locator: Appendix G Repeats and error bars
